pages.text: Kota's home was a mountain hot-spring inn. Each morning, Dad scrubbed the bath stones with a brush. Steam puffed from every pool—guests would come today, too. Kota hopped around the yard without looking at the steam.
A tall crane stepped through the gate. "A long journey left me stiff and cold. I'd like to soak in just the right bath." "I know! Here!" Kota pointed to the nearest doorway.
The crane dipped a toe, then jumped. "Too hot!" Kota's face turned red. "Actually... I don't know which bath is hot."
Dad crouched beside Kota and pointed. "See that steam? It tells us. Shall we play Gentle Steam, a Fingertip Dip?" "I'm curious, too," the crane said, stretching his neck.
Thin steam drifted gently from the lower pool. Kota dipped a fingertip. "Warm!" Dad nodded. "Gentle steam means warm."
Thick clouds billowed from the upper pool. Kota quickly hid their hands behind their back. "Billowing means too hot! Even fingertips need care!"
Kota watched the middle pool. "Gentle steam! This one's right!" The crane tested with a fingertip and eased in. "Ah, perfect!" Kota's tail shot skyward.
"You're a bath expert!" The crane splashed lightly. Kota's cheeks glowed, shoulders lifting proudly. "I'll find one for the next guest, too!"
Now Kota counted aloud before a bath. "One, watch the steam! Two, dip a fingertip! Three, welcome in!" The crane smiled from the water.

At night, gentle steam rose beside the baths. Dad sat Kota on his lap and wrapped their shoulders in a dry towel. "It's all right not to know. Look first, and you'll learn." Kota smiled. "Tomorrow, Gentle Steam, a Fingertip Dip!"
